root_cause.text: The SMB Direct server in `fs/smb/server/transport_rdma.c` used a race-prone credit accounting scheme based on `recv_io.posted.count` and `credits.count`, so `manage_credits_prior_sending()` could grant receive credits after the peer had already consumed them but before `recv_done` updated state, causing over-granting of non-existent credits.
root_cause.evidence: The patch message explicitly says “The logic off managing recv credits by counting posted recv_io and granted credits is racy” and explains “between receiving the incoming recv at the hardware and processing the completion in the 'recv_done' functions we likely have a window where we grant credits, which don't really exist”; the fix adds a separate `sc->recv_io.credits.available` counter, incremented when receive buffers are posted and drained when credits are granted, and changes `manage_credits_prior_sending()` to use `atomic_xchg(&sc->recv_io.credits.available, 0)` instead of deriving credits from `posted.count`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix receive credit accounting by updating the available credits counter before triggering follow-up work.
intent_record.what: The function `smb_direct_post_recv_credits()` now adds the local `credits` count to `sc->recv_io.credits.available` using `atomic_add()` before the existing conditional `queue_work()` call.
intent_record.how: At runtime, any receive credits calculated in this worker are now recorded in the shared available-credit counter, ensuring the system's credit accounting reflects newly posted credits before potentially scheduling more immediate work.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix credit accounting so only the needed and available credits are granted, while preserving any leftover available credits for later.
intent_record.what: The function manage_credits_prior_sending() was changed to introduce local variables missing and available, replace the previous posted.count-based credit calculation with a computation based on credits.target minus credits.count, atomically fetch-and-clear credits.available via atomic_xchg(), compute new_credits using min3(U16_MAX, missing, available), and add logic to restore any unused available credits back into credits.available when no credits are granted or when only part of the available credits are consumed. A comment was also added to note that granted credits are remembered by incrementing credits.count.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now grants send/receive credits only up to the remaining target deficit and only from the pool of currently available credits, while preserving any excess available credits for later use. This prevents losing credits when there are available credits that cannot all be granted immediately, and makes the credit accounting more accurate and robust.

grouping_result.intent: Fix credit accounting so only the needed and available credits are granted, while preserving any leftover available credits for later.

consistency_review.core_intent: Fix receive credit accounting so only the needed and available credits are granted, while preserving any leftover available credits for later.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the vulnerable receive credit accounting logic in SMB Direct. It changes how credits are counted and granted to avoid over-granting based on stale state, which matches the race-prone credit accounting root cause.

candidates.rationale: This reads the total posted receive count as the basis for granting credits, which is race-prone because it can become stale relative to peer consumption and recv_done updates.
This subtraction uses a potentially stale credits counter to decide how many credits to grant, which can over-grant credits when peer activity races with accounting updates.
This commits the computed grant into the shared credits counter; if the computed value is based on stale state, it directly causes over-accounting and granting of non-existent credits.
This check relies on the current credits count as the gating condition, but the root cause is that the count can lag behind actual receive completion and lead to incorrect credit grants.

vuln_statements.explanation: This uses the total posted receive count as the basis for credit grants, which can be stale relative to peer consumption and recv_done updates, leading to over-granting.
This subtracts a potentially stale credits counter from the posted count, allowing manage_credits_prior_sending() to compute and grant more credits than actually exist.
This commits the stale, race-prone computed grant into the shared credits counter, directly causing over-accounting and granting non-existent receive credits.
This gating check depends on the current credits count, which can lag behind actual receive completion and contribute to incorrect credit grants under race.
